title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Acceptance and Booking Status for Amendment Fees
content:
## Clause

An amendment fee on a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file can arise only where two statuses allow it at the same time. The acceptance must stand as submitted, under review or approved. And the booking carrying the goods must not show them as loaded; the statuses that show this are requested, confirmed, equipment released and gated in, referred to here as the pre-loading statuses. Once the booking shows loaded, departed, closed or cancelled, the goods on it carry no amendment fee.

The re-review fee is not priced by this rule; it can still be entered only on an acceptance that is submitted, under review or approved.

## Status grid for the amendment fee

| Acceptance status | Booking status | Amendment fee can arise |
|---|---|---|
| submitted, under review or approved | requested, confirmed, equipment released or gated in | yes |
| submitted, under review or approved | loaded, departed, closed or cancelled | no |
| loaded, discharged, closed, rejected or withdrawn | any status | no |

## Where the evidence sits

The acceptance and the booking are separate records. Whether the goods have gone on board is read from the booking's own status, and that status decides whether an amendment fee can arise at all.

## Points of judgement

**The booking shows gated in. Can an amendment fee still arise?** Yes; gated in is one of the booking statuses that still permit it.

**The acceptance is approved but its booking shows departed.** No amendment fee arises on those goods.
